# QuicKcals

> A calorie and macro diary that works out what you ate from a photo, a
> barcode or a sentence, learns what you actually burn, and judges you on the
> trend rather than on any single day.

QuicKcals is a web app (a PWA — it installs from the browser on iPhone and
Android, with no app store involved). It is built for people who have tried a
food diary before and stopped, so the design goal throughout is fewer taps per
meal rather than more features.

## What it does

- **Log a meal three ways.** Photograph the plate, scan a barcode, or type what
  you ate in plain English ("two rashers of bacon and a slice of toast"). The
  AI estimate is itemised, and it shows the portion it assumed so a wrong guess
  is a one-tap correction rather than a reason to give up.
- **Tells you what you actually burn.** Most trackers use a formula and never
  revisit it. QuicKcals compares what you logged against what your weight
  actually did, and corrects its own estimate of your burn from the result. A
  connected WHOOP replaces that estimate with a measurement.
- **Trend weight, not scale weight.** Day-to-day weight is mostly water. The
  app shows a smoothed trend and projects it against your goal.
- **Marks its own confidence.** Anything from a barcode or a food database is
  labelled verified; anything the AI estimated is labelled an estimate. The app
  never presents a guess as a fact.
- Also: saved meals and recipes, macros, keto mode, a fasting timer, body
  measurements and progress photos, a weekly review, offline logging, and a
  full export of everything you have ever entered.

## Pricing (GBP, UK)

- **Free — £0.** The whole diary: unlimited barcode scans, food search, saved
  meals, recipes, every chart and your full history. Three AI estimates a day.
  Shows ads. Not a trial — it does not expire and does not ask for a card.
- **Plus — £4.99/month or £44.91/year.** No ads, photo logging, ten AI
  estimates a day, fasting timer, keto mode, measurements and progress photos,
  eating window, weekly review.
- **Pro — £9.99/month or £89.91/year.** Everything in Plus, forty AI estimates
  a day, recipe and label scanning, WHOOP integration for measured burn, and
  the weekly report filed to your Drive.

Cancel from Settings in two taps via Stripe's own portal. Full refund if asked
for within 14 days.

## Things it deliberately does not do

- **No live Apple Health or Health Connect sync.** Neither can be read by a
  website — they are native-only. QuicKcals reads the export file those apps
  produce and imports your weight history from it, free on every plan. Any
  claim of a live connection would be false.
- **No meal plans and no telling you what to eat.** It is a record, not a
  coach, and it is not medical advice.
- **No selling or sharing of diary data.** See /privacy.html.

## Guides

Plain explanations of the things a food diary usually leaves unsaid. Written
by the people who build the app, and honest about what nobody can measure
precisely.

- Why the scale lies: https://quickcals.com/guides/why-the-scale-lies
  A kilogram of fat is about 7,700 kcal, so an overnight kilo is water,
  glycogen and food in transit. Why weighing daily and reading a trend beats
  weighing weekly.
- What you actually burn in a day: https://quickcals.com/guides/what-you-actually-burn
  Calorie calculators output a population average. How to derive your own
  maintenance from four weeks of your own intake and weight trend.
- How wrong is your calorie count: https://quickcals.com/guides/how-wrong-is-your-calorie-count
  Label tolerances, portion estimation, and why a consistent error cancels out
  of the arithmetic that matters.
- Logging food you didn't cook: https://quickcals.com/guides/logging-food-you-didnt-cook
  Estimating a restaurant plate from components, where restaurant calories
  hide, and why a rough entry beats none.
- Why the weight stopped moving: https://quickcals.com/guides/why-the-weight-stopped-moving
  Logging drift, water masking fat loss, and a genuinely lower maintenance —
  how to tell which one a plateau is.
